# fptcloud_object_storage_iam_user_access_key (Resource)



## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "fptcloud_object_storage_iam_user" "example" {
  vpc_id      = "your_vpc_id"
  region_name = "your_region_name"
  user_name   = "app-backend"
}

# An IAM user may hold at most two access keys. Keeping the second one in the
# configuration is what makes a rotation possible without an outage: create it,
# move the consumers across, then remove the first.
resource "fptcloud_object_storage_iam_user_access_key" "example" {
  vpc_id      = "your_vpc_id"
  region_name = "your_region_name"
  user_name   = fptcloud_object_storage_iam_user.example.user_name
}

# The secret is returned only when the key is created and can never be read
# back, so it lives in the Terraform state from that moment on. Treat the state
# as a secret store, and mark any output that exposes it as sensitive.
output "access_key_id" {
  value = fptcloud_object_storage_iam_user_access_key.example.access_key_id
}

output "secret_access_key" {
  value     = fptcloud_object_storage_iam_user_access_key.example.secret_access_key
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `region_name` (String) The region name that's are the same with the region name in the S3 service. Currently, we have: HCM-01, HCM-02, HN-01, HN-02
- `user_name` (String) Name of the IAM user the access key belongs to
- `vpc_id` (String) The VPC ID

### Read-Only

- `access_key_id` (String) The access key ID
- `created_at` (String) When the access key was created
- `created_by` (String) The portal user that created the access key
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `secret_access_key` (String, Sensitive) The secret access key. The API returns it only when the key is created, so it is recorded in state at that moment and can never be recovered afterwards - a lost secret means a new key
